summary: The claim holds. /premium?redirect=... is produced by the router guard and by the LearningPath CTA but no code anywhere in frontend/src reads the param back, and a real guest/non-premium bounce followed by a real login lands on /lessons, not the requested route.

producers: frontend/src/components/home/LearningPath.test.js:38 -> asserts the href '/premium?redirect=%2Fspeaking' is produced (test only locks the producer, not any consumer)
static_evidence.grep: grep -rn 'redirect' frontend/src (excl node_modules) returns exactly 5 matches: the 3 above + router/index.js:178 'redirect: /admin/dashboard' + router/index.js:193 'redirect: /' (both are static vue-router redirect config, unrelated).
static_evidence.query_redirect_reader_grep: grep -rn 'query.redirect|URLSearchParams|location.search|params.redirect|redirect=' frontend/src -> only the 2 producers. PremiumCheckout.vue:57 reads route.query.plan (not redirect). PremiumPage.vue has no useRoute at all.
static_evidence.global_hooks: frontend/src/router/index.js defines only beforeEach (line 202). No afterEach, no scrollBehavior. frontend/src/main.js and frontend/src/App.vue contain no route/redirect handling.
static_evidence.login_landing: frontend/src/views/Login.vue:68 -> router.push('/lessons') unconditionally; frontend/src/views/Register.vue:96 -> router.push('/lessons') unconditionally.

live_evidence.stack: frontend http://localhost:5173 (Vue dev), backend http://localhost:8080, Playwright chrome-devtools MCP, isolated browser contexts
live_evidence.rate_limit_flush: docker exec engflow-redis redis-cli --scan --pattern 'rate_limit:*' | xargs del (before HTTP batch)

probe_account.created_via: real UI registration at /register (real backend POST /api/auth/register)
probe_account.cleanup: DELETE FROM users WHERE user_id = 201747; -> 1 row, verified by listed id (not LIKE). parity restored to 1470|43735|72|118|29|15|4|126|10|5 (72 users = baseline).

steps.action: guest navigates to /speaking (no token in isolated context)
steps.meaning: guard bounce reproduces live; producer emits the param

steps.action: cleared localStorage/sessionStorage, then real non-premium user (isPremium=false in stored user) navigates to /speaking
steps.result: location = http://localhost:5173/premium?redirect=/speaking ; stored user isPremium=false ; page shows Premium pricing; no /speaking content
steps.meaning: bounce also reproduces for a logged-in non-premium user

steps.action: exact claimed flow: guest bounced to /premium?redirect=/speaking, then navigates to /login and submits real credentials for the non-premium probe account
steps.result: location after login = http://localhost:5173/lessons ; search = '' ; loggedIn=true ; isPremium=false ; h1 = 'Bài học'
steps.meaning: the user is NOT returned to /speaking. The param is discarded. Claim's core assertion proven live.

skeptic_checks.probe_artefact_429: ruled out - all probes used the Vue dev server routing (client-side guard) and one real login; no rate-limit 429 observed; buckets flushed before the batch
skeptic_checks.guard_redirect_misread: ruled out - the redirect target itself is the evidence (the query param is present in location.search), and the absence of any consumer is independently proven by source grep, not by a redirect being read as failure
skeptic_checks.correct_behaviour_question: No. The param is emitted with the clear intent of a post-login return (LearningPath CTA 'Xem Premium' even pre-encodes /speaking), but nothing consumes it. This is dead code / broken intent, not intentional design.
skeptic_checks.severity_justification: LOW is correct. No security, data-loss, or access-control impact. No user is blocked; every affected route is a premium paywall a non-premium user cannot enter anyway. The only loss is a post-login convenience redirect. It is a real, reproducible UX defect, hence not refuted.

notes_for_panel: The finding is accurate and reproducible. The only nuance a fix author should know: the param is doubly dead because both Login.vue and Register.vue hardcode router.push('/lessons'), so even wiring a consumer in a premium component would not help - the fix belongs in the auth landing path (or a global beforeEach consumer) plus PremiumCheckout's post-activation push (PremiumCheckout.vue:87 pushes '/speaking' hardcoded).
